subject: Capacity onramp playbook: 8→16 GPU reservation and throughput warranty
messages:
From: Courtney Lee <courtney.lee@NimbusCloud.io>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: sales-ops@nimbuscloud.io
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + 8→16 upgrade — initial ask and timing

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the renewal conversation earlier — Nimbus is evaluating a bump from an 8-GPU reserved pool to 16 GPUs as part of our Nov–Dec go-live. We want to lock a monthly commit that reflects the 2x capacity and get a documented throughput warranty for production traffic (peak concurrency guarantees and a KV cache sizing recommendation).

High-level ask:
- Start date: 2026-12-01 (target)
- Monthly commit: increase from current baseline to a $60k/mo equivalent (we included rough numbers in the attached order form)
- Throughput warranty: 95th percentile token latency targets and a minimum sustained throughput per GPU across burst windows
- Ramp: staged activation over two weeks with a rollback window

Can your team share a simple activation playbook and confirm whether Redwood can provide a signed SLA addendum for throughput? We need this for our procurement and SRE sign-off.

Appreciate it — can we schedule a short ops alignment call this week?

Courtney
Account Lead, Nimbus Cloud

Attachments: Nimbus_ONRAMP_v2_OrderForm.pdf
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Courtney Lee <courtney.lee@NimbusCloud.io>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + 8→16 upgrade — initial ask and timing

Courtney — thanks for the clear asks and the form. Looping in David (Account Ops) and Marissa (Capacity/Oncall) to scope the playbook and SLA. Quick answers up front:

- Target start looks feasible for 2026-12-01 if contract is signed by 11/15 and activation artifacts are provided.
- We can model a monthly commit that maps to the capacity you sent; I'll have David confirm the exact $ amount after we map usage patterns.
- Redwood can commit to a throughput warranty as an addendum. We typically warranty 95th percentile token latency and sustained throughput per pipeline stage; final numbers depend on model variant and prefix cache hit rates.
- We recommend a staged activation: warm-up (3 days), scale (7 days), verify (4 days). Full rollback plan included in the playbook we’ll share.

I'll take point on putting together a short ops playbook and a draft SLA addendum for your procurement. Can we do a 30-minute call on Thu 10/29 at 10:00 PT?

—Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

That time works — calendar invite incoming. Two quick clarifications before the call so we can prepare:
- We run a mix of two model families (Llama-2 derived and a proprietary seq2seq). Can Redwood provide separate throughput guarantees per model family?
- Billing question: if activation happens mid-cycle, can we prorate the first month and align subsequent invoices to the calendar month? Procurement prefers month-aligned invoices.

I’ll also share our current peak concurrency window sample.

Courtney

Great chat earlier — notes and next steps below. (Follow-up to the 10/29 call.)

Call recap (short):
- Models: we will produce a per-family throughput profile. For Llama-2 derivatives we can commit to X tokens/s/GPU (profile attached). For your seq2seq variant, we'll run a short perf test during the warm-up to finalize numbers.
- Billing: Redwood can prorate the activation month and then invoice calendar-month cycles going forward. We will include pro-rate language in the order form and standard invoice alignment in the SOW.
- Activation timeline: sign by 2026-11-15 → enable staging cluster 11/20 → warm-up window 11/30–12/02 → full shift 12/03–12/10. Rollback guardrails defined (traffic cut to 8-GPU baseline).
- SLA addendum: draft will include a throughput warranty (95th pct latency), a remediation credit table, and a requirement list (prefix cache config, KV sizing, and a minimal request shaping policy).

Action items:
- Olga: send draft SLA + playbook by 2026-11-02 (attached).
- David: confirm monthly commit dollar amount and update order form.
- Marissa: ops runbook + escalation contacts.
- Courtney: share peak concurrency sample and procurement timing.

Attachments: Throughput_Warranty_SLA-2026-11.pdf, activation-playbook-8to16.docx

—Olga

Subject: Re: Capacity onramp playbook: 8→16 GPU reservation and throughput warranty

Hi all — I ran the numbers against Nimbus’s usage profile (Courtney’s sample) and mapped it to an updated monthly commit. Proposed commit: $58,500/month, which includes:
- 16-GPU reserved pool (baseline throughput targets baked in)
- One-time activation fee (prorated on first invoice)
- Two weeks of dedicated onboarding support (Ops/Engineering)

Notes: the $58.5k figure assumes a 60% prefix cache hit rate during steady state and the Llama-2 family for 70% of traffic. If the seq2seq perf test shows lower cache hit rates, the commit may shift up ~8–12%.

Courtney — if this maps OK to your procurement thresholds, we can embed the figure in the order form and circulate for signature. Happy to jump on a quick pricing call if needed.

David

We can accept the pro-rated first invoice and calendar alignment. If you can confirm acceptance of the two tweaks, we’ll return a countersigned order by 11/12.
